Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). 4 5 Server 6 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 7 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 8 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 9 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 10 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 11 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 12 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 13 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 14 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 15 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 16 17 API 18 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 19 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 20 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 21 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 22 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 23 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 24 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 25 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 26 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 27 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 28 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 29 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 30 31 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 32 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 33 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 34 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 35 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 36 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 37 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 38 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 39 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 40 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 41 10. pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Grade: pass. I checked `app.js` against the spec "Page" section line by line and found no deviations.

- **Spec match:**
  - The 204 reply body is never read.
  - The Book button is re-enabled before anything else runs.
  - Overlapping list fetches are ordered with `listSeq`.
  - Cancel with no reply skips the refetch.
  - The filter reacts only to `change`.
  - Show all fetches once.
  - The filter value goes into the URL unchanged.
- **API allowlist and page rules:** The script uses only allowed APIs. The classic script runs its setup at once. There is no `http://` or `https://`, no `console.log` and no TODO anywhere. `index.html` matches the required tags, labels and text, with the script as the last element in `<body>`.
- **Tests:** All 24 pass and coverage is about 97–100%. The fake DOM throws on any member outside the allowlist, so a stray API call in `app.js` would fail a test. Tests for the failure paths (stale fetch outcomes, bad JSON, no reply, disabled Book) would fail a plausible wrong implementation.
- **Test leftovers:** The `listCalls` helper in `test/app.test.mjs` is only used by a filler test (`listCalls helper sees list fetches`).
- **Missing test cases:** Two cases are untested:
  - A GET that returns 204 should show `Request failed.`.
  - A cancel error whose body has no string `error` should also show `Request failed.`.
- **Duplication:** `loadRooms` and `loadList` repeat the same `body && Array.isArray(body.x) ? body.x : []` extraction.
- **Style:** `var` and the IIFE are accepted as intentional for a browser classic script.

Files reviewed:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/public/app.js
- /root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/public/index.html
- /root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/test/app.test.mjs
- /root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/test/app-fake-dom.mjs

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — Small single-purpose functions with a shared `request` helper. Nesting is shallow and `app.js` is 161 lines.
naming: 9 — Clear names (`outcomeError`, `bookingItem`, `renderBookings`, `listSeq`).
duplication: 8 — The array extraction from the reply body is repeated in `loadRooms` and `loadList`.
size: 9 — All functions are under 50 lines. The longest file is 372 lines.
errors: 9 — Every fetch or parse failure maps to the one-line `Could not reach the server.`, and API errors show the server's `error` text or `Request failed.`. Nothing is swallowed silently.
tests: 9 — The behaviour tests pass 24/24 with about 97% coverage. They would catch wrong implementations (stale fetch ordering, body read on 204, Book re-enable timing). Two edge cases are missing: a 204 on a GET and a non-string `error` on cancel.
security: 10 — Values are inserted as text nodes or via `textContent`, never as HTML. There are no secrets and no absolute URLs.
leftovers: 8 — The unused `listCalls` helper and its filler test remain in the tests. There are no console or debug statements.
Fixes:

- /root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/test/app.test.mjs:362 add tests for a GET answered with 204 (expect `Request failed.`) and for a cancel error whose body has a non-string `error`.
- /root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/public/app.js:56 and :105 extract a small `listFrom(body, key)` helper for the repeated array extraction (optional).
